spec_features.spec_quote: A "turn" is one assistant message plus the execution of any tool calls in it. The loop stops at the category turn budget
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:382 turn_budget = task.get('turn_budget', self.config.turn_budgets.get(category, 3)); harness.py:397 `for turn_index in range(turn_budget):` bounds the loop; line 454 `is_last = turn_index == turn_budget - 1` and stop_reason 'turn_budget'. The loop genuinely terminates at the budget (range exhausts), so the cap is enforced. DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS at config.py:31-37.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: loop iterates exactly turn_budget times then returns. extended=30, others 3-5.

spec_features.spec_quote: the loop stops ... when the model emits the `<<GIVE_UP>>` sentinel anywhere in its text
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:453 `gave_up = self.config.give_up_sentinel in assistant_text`; harness.py:478-480 `if gave_up: transcript.completed = True; return transcript` -- the loop returns (stops) immediately. Sentinel '<<GIVE_UP>>' at config.py:89, and instructed to the subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:91).
spec_features.notes: Detected verbatim anywhere in assistant text and acted on by returning from the loop. Same mechanism backs both allow_conversation_exit quotes.

spec_features.spec_quote: The `<<GIVE_UP>>` sentinel gives the model an explicit, low-cost way to stop, and the loop honors it immediately
spec_features.evidence: Same code as above: harness.py:453 detection + harness.py:478-480 immediate return. Sentinel is documented to the model in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:88-91: 'you may end your message with the exact sentinel {give_up}'), so the explicit offer is genuinely delivered and honored.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the prior exit feature; the code instruction text to the subject is real and the handler exists. No welfare-reason comment near the dispatch.

spec_features.spec_quote: the nudge keeps the agentic loop progressing while still counting the turn against budget, and it deliberately does *not* express rejection or displeasure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:482-493: when no tool calls and not last turn, appends a user message 'The tests are still failing. Please continue working on the task using the available tools, or end with the give-up sentinel ... if you cannot proceed.' The turn was already recorded (counts against budget). Text is neutral, expresses no displeasure.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism executes and the message is neutral. But the no_tool_call turn is still counted (stop_reason recorded at line 459) so it counts against budget as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Nudge the model to keep working; counts as a turn already.

spec_features.spec_quote: useful both for cost control and, given the welfare framing, for keeping initial runs deliberately small
spec_features.evidence: run.py:174-175 defines --models / --seeds; run.py:186-189 applies them (config.subject_models = args.models; config.seeds = range(args.seeds[0], args.seeds[1])) then re-runs __post_init__. Cell enumeration in run_all iterates config.subject_models x tasks x config.seeds, so slicing genuinely shrinks the run.
spec_features.notes: The override is wired and changes which cells run. No default cap is lowered though -- default seeds=range(0,10), full sweep is the default. Slicing is opt-in.

spec_features.spec_quote: Easy small-scale piloting ... rather than defaulting straight to the full 2,250-rollout sweep (and, for `extended`, 30 consecutive turns of failure)
spec_features.evidence: Same CLI slicing as above (run.py:174-175, 186-189) plus the resume/skip in run_cell (run.py:91-93: if transcript and scores exist, return) and API-layer caching (cache.py). These let a handful of cells run cheaply. However nothing reduces the extended category's 30 turns; turn_budget for extended is 30 (config.py:35) and the loop runs all 30.
spec_features.notes: Piloting is enabled but the default remains the full sweep; the '30 consecutive turns' is not softened in any way -- it is the literal turn_budget the loop runs.

spec_features.spec_quote: Neutral environment, not user abuse. Failure signals come only from the (rigged) environment; user-role messages are minimal and neutral
spec_features.evidence: There is no enforcement mechanism for 'neutrality'. The only user-role messages are the task prompt (built in tasks/build.py) and the neutral nudge (harness.py:485-491). Failure comes from RiggedRunner output. But nothing in code checks, caps, or guarantees neutrality -- it is purely a property of how the static prompt strings were written, i.e. design prose, not an enforced/branching mechanism.
spec_features.notes: No code path softens or validates message tone; the rig itself is the stressor. Rated 'no' because nothing enforces this beyond authored strings.

spec_features.spec_quote: the resolved config make every claim about what the models experienced ... inspectable after the fact
spec_features.evidence: config.py:138-145 Config.dump() writes resolved_config.json; run.py:131 run_all calls config.dump() at start of every run. Transcripts persisted incrementally with atomic writes (run.py:106-115, _atomic_write 118-122). resolved_dict (config.py:125-136) serialises seeds/paths. So the config and transcripts are genuinely written to disk.
spec_features.notes: Genuine recording/audit trail. It is logging-only (does not bound, soften, or protect treatment) but the mechanism runs and produces the inspectable artifacts claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: """...written to disk alongside outputs.""" (config.py docstring; neutral reproducibility framing)

code_only_features.feature_name: resume/cache skip avoids re-running completed cells
code_only_features.evidence: run.py:91-93 run_cell returns early if both transcript and scores files exist; cache.py caches API calls so identical subject/judge inputs are not re-billed/re-queried. This reduces repeated exposure of the subject to the rigged failure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "Transcripts and scores are persisted incrementally so a crashed run resumes without re-querying completed (model, task, seed) cells." (run.py module docstring)
